newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cheung Tai in HK$231 mln property deal.
newsitem.headline: Cheung Tai in HK$231 mln property deal.

text.p: Cheung Tai Hong Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday it will pay a total of HK$231.27 million to buy a stake in two property projects in Hong Kong and Shenzhen from its controlling shareholders.
The company will issue 200 million new shares at HK$0.62 per share to finance the deals with the remaining balance funded by internal resources, it said in a statement.
Cheung Tai Hong agreed to buy a 48.73 percent stake and a shareholder's loan in Shenzhen Rainbow Shopping Co from its chairman Wong Chun Hong and his associates for HK$56.13 million.
The purchase price represents six times Shenzhen Rainbow's unaudited after-tax profit but before extraordinary items of 20.55 million yuan for the year ended December 31, 1996.
Shenzhen Rainbow owns two department stores and a franchise for the operation of another department store in Shenzhen.
Cheung Tai Hong said Wong has guaranteed that if Shenzhen Rainbow reported profit of less than 20.55 million yuan for the year ending December 31, 1997, he would pay the shortfall.
Cheung Tai Hong also said it had agreed to take a 60 percent stake in Master Super Development Ltd for HK$175.14 million.
Master Super has agreed to buy properties on Hong Kong island for a total of HK$291.90 million.

Primestone Enterprises Ltd, owned by Wong and Cheung Tai Hong vice chairman Hui Kwok Wai, has agreed to place 200 million existing shares with private investors at HK$0.62 per share, before subscribing to the new shares.
Its stake in the company will be diluted to 52.0 percent, from 62.7 percent after the placement and new share issue.
Cheung Tai shares rose HK$0.03 to HK$0.81 in Tuesday morning trade.
